Treat the two conjuncts independently.

- For the first, let \(i:\{x // x\in t\}\to\alpha\) be the subtype inclusion and \(f=X\circ i\). By the defining neighborhood property of the coinduced topology along \(f\), the assumption \(s\in\mathcal N(Xa)\) implies
  \[
  f^{-1}(s)\in\mathcal N(\langle a,h\rangle).
  \]
  Translate neighborhoods in the subtype into neighborhoods within \(t\) in \(\alpha\). Since \(f^{-1}(s)\) is the subtype restriction of \(X^{-1}(s)\), this yields
  \[
  X^{-1}(s)\in\mathcal N[t](a).
  \]
  The hypothesis \(h:a\in t\) is essential for forming the subtype point whose image is \(Xa\).

- For the second, use the characterization
  \[
  x\in\operatorname{interior}(s)\iff s\in\mathcal N(x).
  \]
  The eventual equality \(s=ᶠ[\mathcal N(x)]t\) allows membership of \(s\) and \(t\) in the same filter to be exchanged. Thus \(s\in\mathcal N(x)\) implies \(t\in\mathcal N(x)\), and the same characterization gives \(x\in\operatorname{interior}(t)\).

Finally combine these two arguments with the constructor for `And`.
